entities.summary:
Wu Zhen was a Chinese painter of the Yuan dynasty, best known for being one of the Four Masters of the Yuan. He was born in unknown and died in 1354. Wu Zhen's work spanned over a decade, during which he created over 300 paintings, mostly of Buddhist scenes.

Wu Zhen's significance lies in his contribution to the Yuan dynasty's artistic development, which blended elements of Chinese and Central Asian styles. His works were highly regarded by his contemporaries and have continued to inspire artists to this day.

Wu Zhen's legacy can be seen in the many museums and galleries that showcase his work, including the Palace Museum in Beijing, which has an extensive collection of his paintings.

One of Wu Zhen's most famous works is his painting of the 'Buddhist Deities in the Garden', which is considered a masterpiece of Yuan dynasty art. The painting is now housed in the National Palace Museum in Taipei, Taiwan.

Wu Zhen's impact on the art world extends beyond his own work, as he helped to establish the Yuan dynasty as a major center of artistic innovation.

Overall, Wu Zhen's contributions to the Yuan dynasty's artistic development and his own remarkable body of work make him one of the most significant artists of his era.
